message:
feat(publish): upload to GitHub Packages with SHA-1 and SHA-256 checksums and no MD5

Gradle's Maven publisher uploads an MD5 and a SHA-1 checksum beside every
file and cannot be told to skip MD5. The publish feature now uploads each
project's staged publications itself, from the repository the Central bundle
is built from: the artifacts, their signatures, and a SHA-1 and a SHA-256
checksum beside each artifact. Never MD5, never a checksum of a signature,
and never maven-metadata.xml, which GitHub Packages regenerates from its own
version records. GitHub Packages answers .md5, .sha1 and .sha256 requests for
any stored file with digests it computes itself, so resolvers can fetch the
same checksums as before; what changes is what a release stores, 20 files
per module with a main, sources and javadoc jar instead of 30. The task's
checksums property changes the set, except that MD5 is never sent.

A PUT the registry answers with 409 fails the upload, as GitHub Packages
versions are immutable, unless it answers a retry of the same PUT, whose
failed attempt had stored the file. Uploads go one version directory at a
time, so a failure leaves at most one version partly uploaded, and 408 and
429 are retried along with 5xx. Maven Central still receives MD5 and SHA-1,
which it requires, through the deployment bundle. sava-build publishes itself
the same way.

Each library project gets uploadToGitHubPackages, which its publish task runs,
as publish did before. The aggregation plugin registers publishToGitHubPackages
over the projects declared with centralPortalAggregation (or nmcpAggregation),
and fails it when there are none rather than passing with nothing uploaded;
the per-project task is named differently so that an unqualified
publishToGitHubPackages still reaches only the aggregation. An aggregation
script written for an earlier version registers its own publishToGitHubPackages
over the savaGithubPackagesPublish repository's tasks; it keeps working
unchanged and uploads the same way, because the plugin then leaves the task to
the script with a deprecation warning, and
publishMavenJavaPublicationToSavaGithubPackagesPublishRepository and
publishAllPublicationsToSavaGithubPackagesPublishRepository remain as deprecated
aliases of uploadToGitHubPackages. To migrate, declare every module the
script's task publishes with centralPortalAggregation, then delete the
registration. The credentials are unchanged (savaGithubPackagesPublishUsername
and savaGithubPackagesPublishPassword). -PsavaGithubPackagesPublishUrl points
the upload elsewhere, which the functional tests use.

Release-As: 21.6.0

feat(scope): build the refresh accounts for an ExponentTranching entry

Refreshing an ExponentTranching entry consumes, after the market, five more
accounts and then the market's get_sy_state accounts, which are resolved through
the market's address lookup table, so ScopeProgramClient could only reject such a
token.

ExponentTranchingMarket.read(address, data), or read(accountInfo), reads what
Scope reads from an Exponent tranching market to build and check its update_market
CPI: the market's lookup table, SY program, return model storage and get_sy_state
list. refreshAccounts(lookupTable) then builds the accounts for one entry on that
market, in the order Scope consumes them: the market and its return model storage,
writable; the lookup table, the SY program, the tranching program's event authority
(EVENT_AUTHORITY) and the program itself (PROGRAM_ID), read-only; then each
get_sy_state account, writable where the market flags it. It refuses a lookup table
other than the market's, and a market whose get_sy_state list asks for a signer,
which Scope cannot provide.

ScopeProgramClient.refreshPriceListExtraAccounts(oracleMappings, tokens,
exponentTranchingAccounts) and refreshPriceList(configuration, oracleMappings,
tokens, exponentTranchingAccounts) take those lists keyed by market. An
ExponentTranching token consumes its market's list in place of its single read-only
account, and every other token is handled as before. A list that does not start with
the token's own market, writable, is refused. The forms without the map still reject
an ExponentTranching token, and their message now points at the builder.

Scope's authors require an entry whose refresh CPIs into another program, as an
ExponentTranching entry's does, to be refreshed in its own single-entry call, since a
failed CPI aborts the whole transaction instead of skipping the entry, so pass such a
token alone. Scope budgets 175,000 compute units for refreshing one, most of a
transaction's 200,000 default.

Kamino Vaults 2.3.0 lets a vault name a permissioning authority. On such a
vault, deposit, depositWithMinSharesOut, buy, buyWithMinSharesOut, withdraw,

feat(scope)!: sync Kamino Scope to the 0.42.0 deploy, add the Canary entry and the new CappedFloored and Token2022Multiplier fields

Kamino Scope was redeployed at slot 451262414 and republished its on-chain IDL
shortly after, still under the version string 0.41.0. The deployed document matches
Kamino-Finance/scope at 03b3dad (release/v0.42.0), and the generated account order
matches the Rust for every builder GroundTruth can compare (12 of 12).

What changed on chain, and what the client now does about it:

- A new oracle type, Canary (51). The mapped account is a Canary PriceFeed and the
  refresh CPIs the canary program's get_price, consuming that program as an extra
  account. ScopeReader parses it as the new Canary entry instead of NotYetSupported.
  ScopeProgramClient.refreshPriceListExtraAccounts still throws IllegalStateException
  for a Canary token, as it already did for the then-unknown ordinal 51; the message
  now names the canary program the refresh needs instead of reporting an unknown type.
- CappedFlooredData carries sources_max_age_s, the age the refresh now allows the
  source and each bound to have. CappedFloored exposes it as sourcesMaxAgeS; zero is
  an entry configured before the field existed, which the program exempts from the
  check, not an absent value. CappedMostRecentOf's existing sourcesMaxAgeS now bounds
  its cap entry as well as its sources.
- Token2022Multiplier entries store daily_auto_approval_bps in the mapping's generic
  data (Token2022MultiplierMappingData). The entry exposes it as
  dailyAutoApprovalBps; zero means every multiplier change suspends the price. A
  mapping update that changes only that value, keeping the entry's type and mint, no
  longer resets its price, so the approved multiplier survives it. The stored price
  data (Token2022MultiplierStoredData) is re-laid: approved_pending_bits and the
  Option<u32> suspension_activation_timestamp are replaced by one Option<u64>
  timestamp whose meaning follows the suspended flag.
- ChainlinkXPriceData is re-laid: activation_date_time is a u32 and an
  Option<u64> approved_multiplier_bits follows it.
- A mapping update now refuses a direct self-reference: a ref price naming its own
  slot (RefPriceSelfReference), a TWAP source naming its own slot
  (TwapSourceSelfReference), and a MostRecentOf, CappedMostRecentOf, CappedFloored,
  MultiplicationChain or PythLazerEMA entry whose sources, cap or floor name its own
  slot, as Conditional already refused. Entries configured earlier are not
  re-validated, and a mutual reference between two slots is still accepted, so
  ScopeReader still has to break such cycles: the back-reference reads as absent in
  the entry graph, null for a single source, cap or floor, while a source list ends
  just before it, and ScopeEntries.referencePrice resolves a reference price
  completely after the walk.
- resume_suspended_price_v2 names the multiplier it approves as an f64. A resume
  records that approval and leaves the entry suspended; the price comes back on the
  next refresh whose oracle carries the approved multiplier, or for
  Token2022Multiplier one within dailyAutoApprovalBps of it. resume_suspended_price
  now answers DeprecatedInstruction (6079), as resume_chainlinkx_price already did;
  both remain in the IDL.
- refresh_chainlink_price now applies the same zero-price refusal (PriceNotValid)
  that refresh_price_list already did.
- Six new errors, 6081 to 6086: RefPriceSelfReference, TwapSourceSelfReference,
  CanaryPriceCPIError, CanaryFeedExpTooLarge, InvalidApprovedMultiplier and
  AutoApprovalBpsOutOfRange.

BREAKING CHANGE: two hand-written records gain a trailing component and their
canonical constructors change arity. CappedFloored(index, sourceEntry, capEntry,
flooredEntry) is now CappedFloored(index, sourceEntry, capEntry, flooredEntry,
sourcesMaxAgeS), and Token2022Multiplier(index, oracle, emaTypes) is now
Token2022Multiplier(index, oracle, emaTypes, dailyAutoApprovalBps). Code that reads
entries through their accessors is unaffected; code that constructs them, or
deconstructs them with a record pattern, adds the new component, 0 where the mapping
predates it. OracleEntry permits a new Canary record, so an exhaustive switch over
OracleEntry needs a Canary arm, and a switch over OracleType a Canary case; the
sealed ScopeError permits six new records, so an exhaustive switch over it needs
their arms too. Three generated records change shape: CappedFlooredData gains a
trailing long sourcesMaxAgeS; ChainlinkXPriceData's activationDateTime narrows to a
u32 read into a long, gains OptionalLong approvedMultiplierBits, and no longer
declares BYTES (its length now depends on the option, use l()); and
Token2022MultiplierStoredData(suspended, approvedMultiplierBits, approvedPendingBits,
suspensionActivationTimestamp) becomes Token2022MultiplierStoredData(suspended,
approvedMultiplierBits, timestamp). ScopeProgram.resumeSuspendedPriceV2 is the
builder to call for a resume; resumeSuspendedPrice still builds but now fails on
chain with DeprecatedInstruction, as resumeChainlinkxPrice already did.

Kamino-Finance/scope at 03b3dad (release/v0.42.0), and the generated account order
matches the Rust for every builder GroundTruth can compare (12 of 12).

What changed on chain, and what the client now does about it:

- A new oracle type, Canary (51). The mapped account is a Canary PriceFeed and the
  refresh CPIs the canary program's get_price, consuming that program as an extra
  account. ScopeReader parses it as the new Canary entry instead of NotYetSupported.
  ScopeProgramClient.refreshPriceListExtraAccounts still throws IllegalStateException
  for a Canary token, as it already did for the then-unknown ordinal 51; the message
  now names the canary program the refresh needs instead of reporting an unknown type.
- CappedFlooredData carries sources_max_age_s, the age the refresh now allows the
  source and each bound to have. CappedFloored exposes it as sourcesMaxAgeS; zero is
  an entry configured before the field existed, which the program exempts from the
  check, not an absent value. CappedMostRecentOf's existing sourcesMaxAgeS now bounds
  its cap entry as well as its sources.
- Token2022Multiplier entries store daily_auto_approval_bps in the mapping's generic
  data (Token2022MultiplierMappingData). The entry exposes it as
  dailyAutoApprovalBps; zero means every multiplier change suspends the price. A
  mapping update that changes only that value, keeping the entry's type and mint, no
  longer resets its price, so the approved multiplier survives it. The stored price
  data (Token2022MultiplierStoredData) is re-laid: approved_pending_bits and the
  Option<u32> suspension_activation_timestamp are replaced by one Option<u64>
  timestamp whose meaning follows the suspended flag.
- ChainlinkXPriceData is re-laid: activation_date_time is a u32 and an
  Option<u64> approved_multiplier_bits follows it.
- A mapping update now refuses a direct self-reference: a ref price naming its own
  slot (RefPriceSelfReference), a TWAP source naming its own slot
  (TwapSourceSelfReference), and a MostRecentOf, CappedMostRecentOf, CappedFloored,
  MultiplicationChain or PythLazerEMA entry whose sources, cap or floor name its own
  slot, as Conditional already refused. Entries configured earlier are not
  re-validated, and a mutual reference between two slots is still accepted, so
  ScopeReader still has to break such cycles: the back-reference reads as absent in
  the entry graph, null for a single source, cap or floor, while a source list ends
  just before it, and ScopeEntries.referencePrice resolves a reference price
  completely after the walk.
- resume_suspended_price_v2 names the multiplier it approves as an f64. A resume
  records that approval and leaves the entry suspended; the price comes back on the
  next refresh whose oracle carries the approved multiplier, or for
  Token2022Multiplier one within dailyAutoApprovalBps of it. resume_suspended_price
  now answers DeprecatedInstruction (6079), as resume_chainlinkx_price already did;
  both remain in the IDL.
- refresh_chainlink_price now applies the same zero-price refusal (PriceNotValid)
  that refresh_price_list already did.
- Six new errors, 6081 to 6086: RefPriceSelfReference, TwapSourceSelfReference,
  CanaryPriceCPIError, CanaryFeedExpTooLarge, InvalidApprovedMultiplier and
  AutoApprovalBpsOutOfRange.

BREAKING CHANGE: two hand-written records gain a trailing component and their
canonical constructors change arity. CappedFloored(index, sourceEntry, capEntry,
flooredEntry) is now CappedFloored(index, sourceEntry, capEntry, flooredEntry,
sourcesMaxAgeS), and Token2022Multiplier(index, oracle, emaTypes) is now
Token2022Multiplier(index, oracle, emaTypes, dailyAutoApprovalBps). Code that reads
entries through their accessors is unaffected; code that constructs them, or
deconstructs them with a record pattern, adds the new component, 0 where the mapping
predates it. OracleEntry permits a new Canary record, so an exhaustive switch over
OracleEntry needs a Canary arm, and a switch over OracleType a Canary case; the
sealed ScopeError permits six new records, so an exhaustive switch over it needs
their arms too. Three generated records change shape: CappedFlooredData gains a
trailing long sourcesMaxAgeS; ChainlinkXPriceData's activationDateTime narrows to a
u32 read into a long, gains OptionalLong approvedMultiplierBits, and no longer
declares BYTES (its length now depends on the option, use l()); and
Token2022MultiplierStoredData(suspended, approvedMultiplierBits, approvedPendingBits,
suspensionActivationTimestamp) becomes Token2022MultiplierStoredData(suspended,
approvedMultiplierBits, timestamp). ScopeProgram.resumeSuspendedPriceV2 is the
builder to call for a resume; resumeSuspendedPrice still builds but now fails on
chain with DeprecatedInstruction, as resumeChainlinkxPrice already did.

fix(core): stop pulling jdk.httpserver into the module graph

http-servers-core declared `requires jdk.httpserver` without using it. The
directive was non-transitive, so it never granted consumers readability — but
resolution follows every requires edge regardless of transitivity, so any
module graph reaching core resolved jdk.httpserver anyway. Consumers on the
Jetty, FusionAuth, or sava backends carried it in their resolved graph and
their jlink images for nothing (~327 KiB, 1.1% of a core-only image).

Removed in d05be43. No source or API change: nothing in core references
com.sun.net.httpserver, and http-servers-jdk declares its own requires.
